title: MMD-Flagger: Leveraging Maximum Mean Discrepancy to Detect Hallucinations
abstract: arXiv:2506.01367v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into agentic AI systems, yet their propensity to generate hallucinations remains a critical safety concern. Detecting these factual errors at test-time, particularly without ground-truth labels, is essential for building trustworthy autonomous agents. We propose MMD-Flagger, an hallucination detection method that utilizes Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) and monitors the stability of LLM outputs across varying decoding temperatures. Our method tracks the MMD trajectory between a LLM's response at a certain decoding configuration and a set of stochastic samples, identifying hallucinations based on the trajectory's characteristic shape. We evaluate MMDFlagger on multi-lingual claim verification benchmarks (MUCH) using modern LLMs like Llama-3 families and Gemma-3.

translated_title: MMD-Flagger：利用最大均值差异检测幻觉
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）日益集成到智能体AI系统中，但其生成幻觉的倾向仍是一个关键的安全隐患。在测试时检测这些事实性错误，尤其是在没有真实标签的情况下，对于构建可信赖的自主智能体至关重要。我们提出了MMD-Flagger，一种利用最大均值差异（MMD）并监测LLM在不同解码温度下输出稳定性的幻觉检测方法。我们的方法追踪LLM在特定解码配置下的响应与一组随机样本之间的MMD轨迹，并根据轨迹的特征形状识别幻觉。我们在多语言声明验证基准（MUCH）上使用现代LLM（如Llama-3系列和Gemma-3）评估了MMD-Flagger。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于最大均值差异（MMD）和输出稳定性监测的幻觉检测方法，通过分析LLM在不同解码温度下的响应轨迹形状来识别幻觉，无需真实标签。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a hallucination detection method based on Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) and output stability monitoring, which identifies hallucinations by analyzing the shape of LLM response trajectories across varying decoding temperatures without ground-truth labels.
